source_text: PREPROCEDURE DIAGNOSIS: Left leg claudication. POSTPROCEDURE DIAGNOSIS: Left leg claudication. OPERATION PERFORMED: Aortogram with bilateral, segmental lower extremity run off. ANESTHESIA: Conscious sedation. The patient was taken to the Angio Suite and placed supine. Both groins were prepped. Local anesthesia was administered in the common femoral artery and, using ultrasound guidance, the common femoral artery was accessed. A guidewire was threaded followed by a 4-French sheath. A 4-French Omni flush catheter was placed. Contrast was administered to identify the level of the renal artery and an aortogram was performed. The catheter was pulled down to the aortic bifurcation and a timed run-off view of both legs was performed. Because of a very abnormal and delayed run-off in the left leg, an isolated left lower-extremity angiogram was performed.
